extraction.name: ScienceQA
extraction.description: A large-scale multimodal dataset containing 21,208 multiple choice science questions from elementary and high school curricula across natural science, social science, and language science, with annotations including lectures and explanations for answers to support chain-of-thought reasoning.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in the SCIENCEQA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. Original science problems were downloaded and individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted based on heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed, answer options were shuffled, and semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Original science problems from IXL Learning's open resources, including questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions that align with California Common Core Content Standards for K-12 education
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in K-12 education. Manual removal of invalid questions (single choice, faulty data, duplicates). Manual revision of incorrect annotations by experts using a data exploration tool.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Manual review and revision of incorrect annotations by experts using a data exploration tool
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of K-12 education
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Semi-automated scripts for reformatting lectures and solutions; heuristic rules for extracting components
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is robust and reliable in distribution as demonstrated by blind studies where Q only and CI only approaches achieved results close to random chance. Performance drops in various component combinations (Q+M only, Q+CT+M only, Q+CI+M only) indicate that all input components provide critical information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for science problem solving benchmarks to diagnose multi-hop reasoning ability and interpretability of AI systems. It can be used for training and evaluating models on science-based question answering with chain-of-thought reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Answer options were shuffled to ensure choices do not follow any specific pattern. Questions were randomly split into training, validation, and test splits with a ratio of 60:20:20. For GPT-3 experiments, training questions were randomly added as exam examples and questions were shuffled and split into batches.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were extracted from original science problems using heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed (questions with only one choice, faulty data, or duplicates). Multiple correct answers were reduced to one. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions to make special structures distinguishable. Incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts. For language models, newline separators in text were replaced with \n. For questions without context, context text was replaced with empty string.
